note: Newest first. Each version's entry is added when main gives the app that version: what is under next, or else the commits that changed the app (docs/RELEASING.md).

next.title: Scenes that change, sound you can hear and move, footage that knits fast
items: Seven ways out: Fade out, Slide out up, down, left and right, Shrink away and Wipe away. The Inspector's Animate section groups the animations into Come in, Go out and Keep moving.

Change scene, on the timeline: at the playhead, what is on screen goes out, a little apart, and what comes next comes in from then, headline first. Before, scenes were only covered by the next one, with their words still underneath.
Select several things and animate them together: they start a little apart, top to bottom, and one Undo takes back the lot.

Checks for words still on screen when the next scene comes in over them, for a part that shows before the box it sits in (a terminal's dots before the window, a button's words after the button sat empty), and for a part left behind when its box goes. Text that something comes in over now counts as gone for reading time.
Footage plays from the start of its file when it comes in, so a clip in a second scene no longer begins part way through. Starts from, in the Inspector, starts it later.

Footage knits several times faster: each clip is copied once at the size it is drawn, and frames are saved with a faster setting that keeps every pixel. In a test with 4K footage, a frame took about 200 ms instead of 600, and every video knits faster.
Hear the voice and music while the timeline plays, with a button to turn it off.
Move a sound, start it later in its file, change its loudness and loop music, from the Voice panel. Music can start at its chorus instead of its quiet opening.
Fit to clips counts the sounds too, so a voiceover is not cut off where the last animation ends.
Your model changes scene with change_scene, and its guide covers exits, scenes, what sits in a box, and where music starts.
Seven pages of the guide said things were not built that are: Yarn, Patterns and the editor, Fill mode, Batch knitting, Motion, Voiceover and Using your model now describe what is there.

entries.title: Post to your own accounts, now or at a time
items: Post a knit to Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Threads, X and YouTube: open it and press Post, or pick several and press Post together for a carousel. Post it now, at a time, or keep it as a draft.

Each platform's limits are checked as you write, before anything is scheduled: X's 280 characters, with a link counting as 23; TikTok taking videos only; the shapes Instagram takes; YouTube's title. A caption too long for one platform gets a field of its own.
A project's new Posts tab shows what went out, with a link to each, what is scheduled, and what needs you. Post a draft now, move a time, or cancel.

Connect your accounts in Settings, Social, through a developer app of your own on each platform. There is no knitted server in between, so your sign-ins stay in your computer's secret store. The new guide, Posting to social accounts, walks through each platform.

Posts go out while knitted is open. One due while it was closed goes out when it opens, if that is within two hours, and otherwise waits as missed for you to post or move. YouTube publishes a scheduled video itself, knitted open or not.

A post that fails before anything was sent, because the network dropped or the platform was busy, is tried again twice. One that fails after says to look on the platform first, so nothing is posted twice.

Instagram and Threads fetch what they post from a public address, so knitted puts each file in a bucket of yours (R2, S3, B2, Spaces, MinIO) or a FileFreak folder just before posting, and removes it after. Test in Settings checks that it works.
TikTok posts follow TikTok's rules for apps: you pick who sees each one, with nothing picked for you, and comments, duets and stitches stay off until you turn them on.
Your model can post too, with schedule_post. What it makes are drafts for you to schedule, unless you let it schedule in Settings, Social.

entries.title: Voices that say it, Briefs that know what is ready
items: A voiceover line can say one thing and caption another. Write the caption after a bar, like Roll it back from the terminal | filefreak sites rollback 3, and the voice says the words, while the screen shows the command. Your model does the same.

The voice no longer reads code aloud without a warning. Check and Knit say when a line reads out a command, a path or a file name, or the command typed on screen, and suggest saying what it does instead.

One take is cut into lines only where the voice really paused, and where each line's length fits its words. Lines it ran together stay one clip, so a word is never split between two, and the voiceover says which lines those are.

Asking your model costs less. It used to check on a voiceover again and again while it was spoken, each time re-reading the whole conversation: 41 of 59 steps in one real ask. Now it waits for the voiceover in one step, and is told to do independent steps at once.

Your model has a copywriting guide: only what the Brief says is true and available now, no invented prices, quotes or reviews, a hook from the reader's own day, and variety across a batch. The posts guide now covers Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Threads and YouTube one by one.

Building the Brief reads your website as a visitor sees it, in the browser, so sections a page draws with JavaScript are read too. notch.fm's Works with band, which says Spotify is planned, used to arrive empty.

The Brief gets today's date and a section for what is available now and what is planned, coming soon or in beta, so nothing planned is written as ready. It suggests as many ideas as the material supports, not always twelve.
Short picture descriptions, like a service's name in a Works with band, are read now; a bare 'logo' still is not.
Music advice is the same everywhere: 0.4 to 0.6 under a voice, since every track is brought to one loudness first.

entries.title: A long list, worked through
items: Keep writing while your model answers: what you send waits its turn under the conversation, and goes when the answer is in. Take any of it out of the queue. If you stop a run, the rest wait for you.

Your model can set how loud the music is under a voiceover. It used to try names for the setting that did nothing; now it is told the name, and a name it gets wrong is refused out loud instead of ignored.
Projects is the first page now, and it and every project's tabs show the knits under way, so you can see what is knitting everywhere at once.
Knits nobody has opened yet say New, and Mark all seen clears them.

Pick several patterns, knits or Yarn files at once: Cmd or Ctrl-click, Shift-click for a run, Cmd or Ctrl+A for everything shown, Escape to clear. Then tag, file, download, duplicate or delete them together.
Ask your model about a pattern, a knit or a file from its own menu: say what to change, and it does it in the chat.
Spending: what your model has cost this month, and a limit that stops it before it goes over.
Copy in Yarn is called Saved text, which says what it is.
Knit at 60 frames a second for fast motion.
Your model reads a guide before it works, topic by topic: patterns, motion, voiceovers, posts and more.
Frames are drawn about three times faster.
Footage in a video no longer stutters. At Story size every third frame used to repeat.
Type-on types a letter at a time, each in its place, and stitch-in brings the words in one by one, each rising into place.

A second animation on the same thing no longer cancels the first, the slow zoom works on video too, and a pulse keeps its beat. Entrances ease in evenly instead of jumping most of the way in the first frames.
Text that slides in is as sharp as a still before and after it moves.
Sound no longer crackles: the finished file's peaks are measured and kept under the limit.
Every voice line and music track is brought to one loudness, music dips once under a voice instead of swelling between words, and music cut off by the end of the video fades out.
Videos come out at the loudness the apps play at, and a knit that does not says so.
Music set too quiet to hear under a voice is flagged, with the level that suits.
Colours in videos match the pattern: a brand red no longer turns orange. Videos also start playing before they have finished loading.
Headlines are balanced over their lines, with no word left alone at the end. Code keeps its indentation, and a pop grows from where the words are.
A short word that starts a sentence stays with the word after it, and a number stays with its unit, so a line no longer ends on a lone "It" or splits "5 GB".
Text that fits its box is no longer reported as cut off: a display font's tall ascent, or a word still rising in, set it off.
Contrast warnings look at what is really behind the words, like a button, a card or a band, instead of the page.
Stories warn when words or a logo sit under the app's top bar or reply bar.
A knit made before its pattern was last changed says so, so an old file is not posted by mistake.
A font knitted does not have, or one that fails to load, is reported instead of quietly drawn in a stand-in.
Website pictures are taken at twice the pixels, so a part cut out of one stays sharp in a post.
Motion checks catch entrances too fast to see, type-on too fast to read, and long stills anywhere in a video, the end included.
Your model can page through every knit in a project, not just the newest 30.

entries.title: Knits under way, in one place
items: Knits under way are one panel instead of a row each: the one knitting, with a bar that fills as its frames are drawn and what it is doing now, and the ones waiting their turn listed under it by name. Cancel any of them, or all at once.

entries.title: See your model at work anywhere
items: While a model works, a card in the corner of every page says what it is doing and what it last wrote, with Show me and Follow. Make it smaller to keep it out of the way.
Follow no longer gets stuck on the page it is leaving: a move that does not land is made again.

Your model can look inside videos now: a sheet of frames from across one, each marked with its time, and a closer look at any part. For audio it gets the length and how the loudness moves. So it can sort and name files whatever they are called.
The chat page no longer scrolls on past the conversation into blank space.
The list of chats can be folded away, for more room to read.

entries.title: Any voice model, used to the full
items: A voice server shows its own voices and models in Settings, including the presets its model has but does not list (Qwen3's Ryan, Serena and the rest). Type any voice name it takes.
Give a style in words ("warm, deep and confident") for models that take one, and any other options your server takes, as JSON.
A voice server's own error now shows in Settings, like an unsupported voice, instead of "Something broke on our side". A model name the server does not have falls back to its own speech model.
A voiceover is spoken in one take, so the voice sounds the same from the first line to the last, then cut at the pauses into a clip per line.
A voiceover's sound now runs to the video's last frame, so a knit no longer refuses it as a few milliseconds short.

entries.title: Captions, hashtags and music for each knit
items: Open a knit and your model writes what goes with the post: a caption in the business's voice, hashtags, and a track from the project's music, with why it fits. It reads the Brief, the post's words and, for a picture, the picture itself.

Write it again as many times as you like, or say what to change first (shorter, more playful, mention Saturday). Edit any of it yourself, pick another track, and copy the caption and hashtags in one go.

entries.title: Sharp pictures
items: Pictures in Yarn and the Brief are sharp in the grid. A tall picture, such as a website page, used to show a small thumbnail stretched; its tile now shows the top of the page.
Choosing a project's picture shows its images as a proper grid of squares, instead of squeezed strips.

entries.title: Videos that play, and room to work
items: A video in a pattern plays now: in the editor, and in the knit. Before, only its first frame showed.
The page no longer scrolls past its end into a blank band.
The editor's top bar keeps its place when a lot is going on: the trail and what your model is doing are cut short, never drawn over each other.
Yarn and Knits show the most used tags, and the rest are in a menu you can search.
With more than one model at work, the side bar shows each one, and you can follow any of them.
A video's thumbnail has a play mark on it.
Knits have tags, to find them by.
The chats are kept apart by project: the Ask page shows one project's chats at a time, and the editor only that project's.

entries.title: A brief for every project
items: A Brief for every project: what your model knows about the business. Sync it with the business's website and knitted reads the public pages, has your model write a profile from them (who they are, what they offer and to whom, how they sound, the facts to get right), and pictures every page on a desktop and a phone. Or write the profile yourself. Your model reads it before it writes, and a change your model makes to it can be undone in the Brief tab.

Give a website when you make a project, and the project starts from it: its swatch read from the site, a profile, and pictures of every page. Sync again at any time to bring all of it up to date: a page pictured before is replaced where it is.

The Brief's reference is a shelf of files to look at and read, like menus, brochures and pictures of the website, kept apart from the Yarn you put in patterns. Move a file between the two with Move to the Brief and Move to Yarn.
PDFs can go in Yarn and the reference. Turn their pages, read their words, and cut a page, or a part of a picture, out as a new picture in Yarn.
Every section can be shown as a grid or a list, sorted and searched: Patterns, Yarn, the reference, Swatch, Parts and Knits. Each remembers its choice on this computer.
One trail at the top of every project page says where you are, from Projects to the folder you are in. Each tab says what it is for, and more buttons say what they do when you point at them.
Your model's replies are formatted, with headings, lists and code, and yours and its are easy to tell apart.
In the editor, the canvas cannot be scrolled or panned out of reach, panning and zooming are gentler, and both side bars fold away (Ctrl or Cmd and \ folds both).

While your model works on a pattern, the stitches it is changing are outlined with its name, and a small bubble over the canvas shows what it is thinking and doing as it happens, even with the chat closed.

New tools for your model: get_brief, set_profile, read_website, capture_website, view_yarn and crop_to_yarn. list_yarn, import_yarn and import_yarn_file take reference: true for the Brief's shelf, and move_to_folder takes referenceIds.
The bundled fonts load in the desktop app on every computer. Before, they failed on any computer but the one the app was built on.
This version adds to your library, and keeps a copy of it from before. An older knitted cannot open the library after that: it says to update.

entries.title: Cards in colour, and one conversation
items: The pattern cards on a project's page show each pattern as the editor draws it, in your swatch's colours and fonts, with your pictures and parts. Before, they were grey outlines. A video's card shows it once everything in it has come in.
Knits show as a grid, each on the same card, whatever its size.

Ask is one conversation, wherever you are. The Ask page opens the chat you are having, and so does the editor's Ask panel when that chat is about the project you are in, or about the whole studio. A message sent from the editor is about the pattern open there. Both list your chats, to open another, and New chat starts a new one in both.
When your model's reply runs past the longest a reply may be, it goes on in smaller steps instead of stopping there.
The sliders in Settings, Model and Voice can be dragged. Before, they would not move. Steps per request now goes up to 100.
Your model can add a file from your computer to Yarn by its path, with import_yarn_file. It copies the file in, leaves yours as it was, and does not read hidden folders or files, such as ~/.ssh.
Your model can bring a piece of copy up to date, instead of saving another beside it, and make an empty folder ready to fill. The project's Activity shows each piece of copy it changes.
get_studio_info tells your model which knitted is answering, when that build was made and when it started, so it can tell you when an older copy is still running.
A project's Activity says in words when a part or a swatch is added, or a file is deleted from Yarn.

entries.title: Ask your model
items: Ask, in the side bar, is a conversation with your model, using your own Anthropic key from Settings, Model. Choose a project for it to work in, or the whole studio, and reply to go on: it reads the whole conversation each time. Your chats are kept, newest first.

While it works you see each step: what it reads, what it changes, and anything a lock refused. Stop ends it. Under each answer is what it changed, with a link to each pattern, and Undo all puts back every pattern that answer changed.
The editor's Ask panel is a conversation about the pattern open in it now, and each project's page has Ask your model.
Stop stops your model in the editor's Ask panel. Before, it went on to the end.

The first time 0.1.5 opens your library, it adds chats to it, after keeping a copy as it was, listed in Settings, Storage. Older versions will not open the library after that, so restore that copy to go back.

entries.title: Folders
items: Sort every section of a project into folders, and folders inside them: Patterns, Yarn, Swatch, Parts and Knits. Make one with New folder, then drag things onto it or choose Move to folder. Rename, move or delete a folder from its menu. Deleting a folder deletes nothing in it: what it held moves up a level.

Whatever you make or add goes into the folder you are in, uploads and pasted screenshots included. A search in Yarn looks in the folder you are in and every folder inside it, and says which folder each file is in.

The editor's Yarn, Parts and Patterns panels show the same folders, and the lists for choosing a file group them by folder. In Knits, Download folder makes a zip with the folders inside it kept as folders.
Your model can sort a project too, with list_folders, move_to_folder and rename, and can put what it makes straight into a folder.
The bar for the browser download no longer jumps back to the start near the end.

The first time 0.1.4 opens your library, it adds folders to it, after keeping a copy as it was, listed in Settings, Storage. Older versions will not open the library after that, so restore that copy to go back.

entries.title: Watch your model work
items: See what your model is doing while it works: its name and what it is doing, in the side bar and in the editor's top bar, with each stitch it changes outlined and named for a moment. Open it for a list of what it did and anything that was refused.
Follow takes you where your model is working and keeps up as it moves. Pause holds its changes until you resume it, and tells it to wait for you.

You and your model can edit the same pattern at once. A change of yours that lands at the same moment as its change is kept, and Undo takes back only your own. Before, the editor reloaded and your last change was lost.
The desktop app downloads the browser it knits with by itself, the first time it starts, instead of waiting for you to press Download it.
check_pattern warns when most of a picture would be cut off because its box is a very different shape, and its low-resolution warning measures the side that is stretched most.
A font in a WOFF2 file is known by its real family name, whatever the file is called, so a brand's own font is found for its swatch.

Your model can make a part from a pattern's stitches, tag Yarn as it adds it, and set the brand's corner radius when it proposes a swatch. Fonts given as {"family": ...} no longer stop a proposal, and a pattern id is enough for every pattern tool.
A model connecting over MCP is told which version of knitted it is talking to, and which tools only read.

entries.title: Knitting in the desktop app, and brands from a website
items: The desktop app downloads the browser it knits with. Before, Download it did nothing, so the app could not knit.
The download shows how far it has got, and says why if it stops. The Knit dialog offers it the first time you knit.
Adding Yarn from a link works in the desktop app, and the file keeps a readable name.

Starting a Swatch from a website finds a brand's real colours far more often: it reads the site in its own dark or light mode and takes the primary colour from its logo. You see where each colour came from and can change it before you create the Swatch, which is not used until you say so.
Your model can propose a Swatch from a website, rename its own drafts and put Yarn into image slots. check_pattern warns about a style that nothing draws.
In Yarn, a search made just after picking a kind shows what it found, not the whole library.
Arrow keys on a slider move the slider. Before, they also moved the selected stitch, when scrubbing the timeline or adjusting a style.
Settings, About shows the version you have.
The desktop app sees a new version as soon as it is out: it reads the list of releases where the installers are kept, not the website's copy.
The Download page puts the newest version first, with every older one below it.
Text on the primary button stays readable when you hover over it.

entries.title: Claude Code, pictures and updates
items: Connect Claude Code from Settings, Model. One command, and it works in knitted with the same tools and locks as the in-app model.
A project can show a picture on its card: one of its images, chosen in Projects, in Yarn, or by your model.
The desktop app updates itself. It asks once whether to check, and Check for Updates is in the menu.
The MCP page and reference list every tool, from the server's own list.

entries.title: Foundations
items: The render engine knits a Pattern frame by frame and encodes it with ffmpeg.
An MCP server lets your model list projects, read a Pattern, fill slots and knit.
Locked stitches are enforced against models. A refused write is reported back, never skipped quietly.
The design system is defined as tokens and shared by the studio and this site.
This site, the docs and the vocabulary: Pattern, Swatch, Yarn, Stitch, Knit and Part.
